signals.title: Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Mini, a 26B open-weights model that runs on a laptop
signals.summary: Thinking Machines released Inkling 2 Mini on Nov 20, a looped transformer with 26.4 billion total parameters and 3.4 billion active per token, running its middle 12 layers three times for every token. The checkpoint is about 20GB and runs on a Mac with at least 32GB of memory or a single DGX Spark, with a 1 million token context window and text plus image input, under the Apache 2.0 license, with weights on Hugging Face and day-zero support in vLLM. The lab says it leads every open-weights model under 100 billion parameters on benchmarks including DeepSWE v1.1 (48.2%) and Vals Index v2.2 (46.5%), and costs about $0.59 per Artificial Analysis task against $3.53 for Qwen3.8-27B. Inkling 2 Small, the 594 billion parameter sibling, stays closed-weight for now pending safety testing, with full weights promised next week. Honest caveats: all benchmark claims are the lab's own, and the looping design is new, so independent results are still to come.
signals.angle: The open model that fits on a laptop just got sharper: a 26 billion parameter model that re-reads its own middle layers three times per token, and the lab says it beats everything its size at coding. Explain looping in one line, the model does more thinking with the same weights instead of adding more weights, then the honest caveat, the scores are the lab's own and the design is brand new, and ask followers whether the future of AI agents is a giant model in a data centre or a small one on your own machine.

signals.title: Bittensor ships runtime 493, its third runtime in five days, making the Yuma emission cap sudo-configurable
signals.summary: Bittensor runtime 493 went live on Nov 20 at block 9,549,497, one day after runtime 492 and four days after 491, the third runtime in five days and the 43rd in 127 days, an average of one every three days. The headline change makes the Yuma timelocked emission cap sudo-configurable, with 37 chain files changed across 42 commits. Spec 494 is already merged and waiting, covering a refund of unused burn payment weight. A follow-up note on Nov 21 added the release's main breaking change, which the original notes had left out: gamma deposits are now spent by their own hotkey at listed subnet services, with the separate spender and GammaSpend proxy removed, so SDK integrators must update before using gamma. Honest caveats: this is a small configuration change, not a feature launch, and the pace itself is the story, three runtimes in five days after the coldkey swap and Gamma work of the previous two.
signals.angle: The follow-up to the runtime 492 post: one day later, another runtime, and the chain now changes about once every three days. Explain the change in one line, the cap on timed emissions can now be adjusted by the sudo key instead of a code release, then the honest caveat, a small config change, not a launch, and ask followers whether a chain that ships this fast is iterating or just patching in public.

signals.title: Orbinum switches on private staking on testnet, hiding who stakes and how much
signals.summary: Orbinum Network, a privacy-focused Layer 1, switched on private staking (ZK-NPoS) on its public testnet: a stake joins a shared pool through a device-built Groth16 zero-knowledge proof with no signature linking a public account, so who stakes and how much stays hidden while pool totals, validators and timing stay public. Confidential pool entry starts at 10 ORB on testnet, unbonding takes about two days, and a disclosure key can reveal a single note without exposing the spending key. Season 1 of its Community Program hands out credits convertible to an airdrop at TGE. Mainnet is targeted for Q4 2026, with a public sale, audits and validator selection still ahead. Honest caveats: testnet only, no mainnet date, no audit results published, no token price, and the chain can reset, so this is a feature demo, not a product yet.
signals.angle: Staking is the most public thing in crypto, every wallet and amount on show, and this testnet hides it. Explain the trick in one line, the proof joins the pool, the signature that would name you never appears, then the honest caveat, testnet tokens are worthless and the mainnet is still a target, not a date, and ask followers whether hidden staking is the privacy feature chains have been missing, or one more thing to audit.

signals.title: Zcash grant proposal would hide which memos your wallet looks up, not just the memos themselves
signals.summary: A $25,000 grant proposal posted Nov 23, titled Private Ironwood Memo Retrieval for iOS Wallets, asks Zcash Community Grants to fund private information retrieval (PIR) for the Zcash iOS SDK, so wallets can fetch encrypted transaction memos without revealing which transaction they are querying. Today even a wallet routed over Tor leaks the transaction IDs it looks up to the server. An iOS Simulator test already retrieved a 512-byte memo through an encrypted query without exposing the transaction ID, and the full application is on the Zcash Community Forum. Full implementation is targeted by Jan 30, 2027, with physical iPhone testing first. Honest caveats: funding is not yet approved, adoption depends on wallet developers shipping the upgraded SDK, and simulator results may not carry over to real devices.
signals.angle: Zcash already hides what you say in a memo. This proposal hides the fact you asked at all. Explain PIR in one line, the server answers your question without learning which question you asked, then ask followers what other lookups leak more than the data itself.

signals.title: OpenRouter off-boards three providers and strips 125 endpoints of Zero Data Retention after prompt theft

Providers Novita, Phala and Together have posted incident reports; OpenRouter says its own systems were not breached and that endpoints must pass assurances and validation before regaining ZDR eligibility. This is the enforcement follow-through to the Dragos canary findings and the MiniMax ZDR pull already on the board.
signals.angle: Zero Data Retention turned out to be a label, not a guarantee, and now OpenRouter is enforcing it by removing providers. Explain the canary trick in plain words, researchers hid unique links in prompts and watched where they got fetched, then ask followers whether they would trust a ZDR badge again without proof.
